input.rationale: Sourced suspicion: appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1241) calls dispatchLogs first, then unconditionally executes r.setLatestConfiguration(configuration, index), r.leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration(configuration) and r.startStopReplication(). dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1279) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns early only on its own error path, so future.Index() is still nonzero and the new configuration is published even though nothing was durably stored. The live configuration is the authority input for quorumSize()/checkLeaderLease() (raft.go:1036-1101), requestVote/requestPreVote admission (raft.go:1603-1813) and the election-start gate in runFollower (raft.go:158-260), so publishing an unpersisted configuration can change the node's own quorum requirement. The harness supplies a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure at the real boundary (storage failure injection) on an otherwise healthy single-voter cluster that had just committed index 3. Observed (CA_EVENT config_publish_after_failed_durable_write): AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned log index 4 is absent from durable storage (getlog_at_assigned_idx_err=log not found, durable_last_index_after=3, raft_last_index=3); yet the node's published configuration now lists two voters (the real one plus phantom/phantom-addr). Observed (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write): after the failure the node never regains leadership over 141 samples/1.5s (state=Candidate, ever_leader_in_window=false) because voters_in_live_configuration=2 sets quorum_size_live=2 while only 1 voter is reachable, so electSelf/preElectSelf can never reach the needed tally. This is conditional evidence: it establishes what the fixed code did for an explicitly supplied transient storage failure; the failure itself is injected, not produced by real producers here. A separate observation from the same run: Raft.GetConfiguration().Index() (api.go:897-906 building configurations{latest:...} without latestIndex, returned by configurationsFuture.Index() in future.go:267-270) reports 0 for this two-voter configuration (config_index_after=0), so the published index of the live authority context is not observable and cannot be used as the prevIndex guard that AddVoter/RemoveServer accept. Unresolved discriminators: whether an equivalent divergence is reachable without storage failure; whether a restart (durable log lacks the entry) is the only recovery path; and the exact set of store-failure timings (pre- vs post-StoreLogs) that produce the divergence.
input.question: When a membership change's durable log write fails, does the leader still publish the new configuration into the live configuration it uses for quorum and election decisions, and can the node still form consensus afterwards?

result.summary: Submitted an `explore` operation (harness: probe_config_publish_test.go) against the hashicorp/raft snapshot at c0dc6a0. Sourced suspicion: appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1241) runs dispatchLogs first and then unconditionally publishes the new membership via setLatestConfiguration + commitment.setConfiguration + startStopReplication, even when dispatchLogs failed to persist the entry (dispatchLogs assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs, so future.Index() is still nonzero). The live configuration is the authority input for quorumSize/checkLeaderLease, requestVote/requestPreVote admission, and the runFollower election gate, so an unpersisted configuration can change the node's own quorum requirement. Local clean-copy execution (in-package Go test, in-memory transport/store, all timing driven by real config, no state injection) supplied one transient failure of the real LogStore.StoreLogs boundary on a just-committed single-voter cluster. Observed: AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned log slot was never durable (log not found, durable last index 3, raft last index 3); yet the node's published configuration now listed a phantom second voter; and the node never regained leadership (141 samples / 1.5s, state Candidate, voters=2, quorum=2, reachable voters=1), i.e. progress stops until a restart. A second observation from the same run: Raft.GetConfiguration().Index() returns 0 (api.go:897-906 leaves latestIndex unset in configurationsFuture, future.go:267-270), so the published index of the live authority context is not observable and cannot serve as the prevIndex guard accepted by AddVoter/RemoveServer. Evidence is conditional (the storage failure is injected, not produced by real producers); the submission records that boundary plus the unresolved discriminators (non-failure reachability, restart-only recovery, exact failure timings). Preflight validation passed (valid: true). No source, evidence, or dependency files were modified; work is limited to draft/probe_config_publish_test.go and draft/submission.json.
